title: Cumulative Review 2: Modules 1 to 6
intro: Spaced review mixes questions from earlier modules. Retrieving older material now is what makes it stick. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: A Type I error occurs when
o: The null is true and we reject it
The null is false and we fail to reject it
The null is false and we reject it
The null is true and we retain it
items.why: A false alarm. Its probability equals alpha when the null is true.

items.q: The central limit theorem says that the distribution of sample means
o: Approaches a normal shape as n increases, whatever the population shape
Has a mean equal to zero
items.why: With n of about 30 or more, the distribution of means is close to normal even for skewed populations.

items.q: A z score for a sample mean is computed as
o: (M minus mu) divided by the standard error
items.why: The standard error replaces the standard deviation because we are locating a mean in the distribution of means.

items.q: A study finds r = +.62 between hours studied and exam score. What proportion of exam score variability is accounted for by study time in this linear relationship?
items.why: .62 squared = .384. The other roughly 62 percent comes from everything else, including prior knowledge and test conditions.

items.q: Participants are randomly assigned to practice a task for 10 or 30 minutes, then tested. Which conclusion is justified if the 30-minute group scores higher?
o: Longer practice caused better performance, subject to sampling error
The groups must have differed in motivation
items.why: Random assignment makes the groups equivalent on average before treatment, which supports a causal claim.

items.q: The mean of the distribution of sample means equals
o: The sample mean of one sample
items.why: Sample means are unbiased. They center on the population mean.

items.q: Standardizing scores makes it possible to
o: Compare scores from different scales on a common metric
items.why: Standardizing changes the units and leaves the shape alone. It does not make skewed data normal.

items.q: A teacher adds 5 bonus points to every exam score. What happens to the mean and standard deviation?
o: The mean rises by 5 and the SD is unchanged
The mean is unchanged and the SD rises by 5
items.why: Every score moves up together, so the center moves and the spread does not.
